Given question: Denise has had COPD for around 10 years and has been coming to your clinic monthly. Recently she has started to gain weight and developed swelling around her ankles. She struggles to breathe and her alveolar ventilation is impaired.What does this ventilation directly depend on? Option A: Airway elasticity, compliance, resistance to air flow, tidal volume Option B: Airway radius, inspiratory reserve volume, resistance to air flow, respiratory rate Option C: Compliance, resistance to air flow, respiratory rate, tidal volume Option D: Distension of air ways, smooth muscle relaxation, resistance to air flow Option E: Distension of air ways, respiratory rate, respiratory rhythm, resistance to airflow The correct answer is Option C.<turn|>
<|turn>model
chosen: The correct answer is C - alveolar ventilation depends on compliance, resistance to air flow, respiratory rate and tidal volume.Airway elasticity - this is part of compliance which is the ability of the lungs to distend Tidal volume - this is the volume of air inhaled or exhaled in quiet breathing Inspiratory reserve volume - this is the max amount air that could be inhaled above the normal tidal volume Resistance to air flow - this is determined by the radius of the air tube and its resistance to distention Respiratory rate - this is the number of breaths per minute Distension of air ways - this is part of compliance which is the ability of the lungs to distend Smooth muscle relaxation - this is important for exhalation to occur more easily Respiratory rhythm - this is the regularity of breathing which is important for alveolar ventilation Airway radius - this is important for resistance to air flow which in turn is important for alveolar ventilation
rejected: Alveolar ventilation = what actually reaches the alveoli, i.e. gas exchange. It is different to minute ventilation which is the volume of air taken in and exhaled. Tidal volume = amount of air taken in and exhaled with each breath. Respiratory rate = number of breaths per minute. Compliance = ability of lungs to stretch. Resistance to air flow = how much the airways resist air moving in and out of the lungs.  COPD is an obstructive disease. This means that the airways are obstructed and so resistance to airflow is increased. This impairs alveolar ventilation. As Denise is struggling to breathe, she may be taking a bigger tidal volume, but there is a limit to how big it can be. She is also taking in more oxygen than she is using up, and this is contributing to her weight gain. This is because she is hyperventilation, and this means her blood vessels are dilating. This leads to her swelling up.
